text: Software Engineering (SE) students following the 2004 and later catalogs must complete ONE application domain, which consists of 3 courses as specified per group; see the Application Domain Information sheet for course groupings. The SE guided elective options (2022-2023) are choices for the remaining SE guided elective. Options and their prerequisites include: CS 4301 Special Topics in Computer Science (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 3345); CS 4314 Intelligent Systems Analysis (prerequisite: CGS 4313 or consent of instructor); CS 4315 Intelligent Systems Design (prerequisite: CGS 4313 or consent of instructor); CS 4332 Introduction to Programming Video Games (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 3345); CS 4334 Numerical Analysis (prerequisite: (MATH 2370 or CE/CS 1337) and MATH 2418, MATH 2451); CS 4336 Advanced JAVA (prerequisite: CE/CS 2336 or equivalent); CS 4337 Organization of Programming Languages (prerequisite: CE/CS 2336 with a C or better, CE/CS 2305 with a C or better, and CS/SE 3340); CS 4341 and CS 4141 Digital Logic and Computer Design and Lab (prerequisite: CE/EE 2310 or CS/SE 3340, PHYS 2326); and CS 4349 Advanced Algorithm Design and Analysis (prerequisite: CS 3305 with a C or better, CE/CS 3345).

text: Additional Software Engineering (SE) guided elective options (2022-2023) include: CS 4352 Human Computer Interactions I (prerequisite: none); CS 4353 Human Computer Interactions II (prerequisite as listed: CS 4325); CS 4361 Computer Graphics (prerequisite: MATH 2418, CE/CS 2336, and CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); CS 4365 Artificial Intelligence (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); CS 4375 Introduction to Machine Learning (prerequisite: CS/SE 3341 and CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); CS/SE 4376 Object Oriented Programming Systems (prerequisite: CE/CS 2336 with a C or better, or equivalent); CS 4384 Automata Theory (prerequisite: CS 3305 with a C or better); CS 4386 Compiler Design (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); CS 4389 Data & Applications Security (prerequisite: CS/SE 4347); CS 4390 Computer Networks (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); and CS 4391 Intro to Computer Vision (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent).

section_heading: Software Engineering Major Guided Elective Options: CS 4352 to CS 4391

text: Further Software Engineering (SE) guided elective options (2022-2023) include: CS 4392 Computer Animation (prerequisite: MATH 2418 and CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); CS 4393 Computer and Network Security (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 4348 or equivalent); CS 4394 Implementation of Modern Operating Systems (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 4348 and CS 3335, or equivalent programming experience); CS 4395 Human Language Technologies (prerequisite: CS/SE 3341 and CE/CS/SE/TE 3345 or equivalent); CS 4396 Networking Laboratory (prerequisite: CS 4390 or equivalent); CS 4397 Embedded Computer Systems (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 4348 or equivalent); CS 4398 Digital Forensics (prerequisite: CE/CS/SE/TE 4348 and CE/CS/TE 4390 or equivalent); CS 4V95 Undergraduate Topics in Computer Science (prerequisite: varies by course topic); and EE 4325 Introduction to VLSI Design (prerequisite: CS 4341). Students may also use SE 4V98 Undergraduate Research in Software Engineering or SE 4399 Senior Honors in Software Engineering. Students must consult an Academic Advisor before registering in these options.
